THE WAVING.CA BUYING GUIDES

Choosing a flagpole for your site

The right pole brings the display, the site and the people operating it together. Use these questions to prepare a useful brief.

IN THIS GUIDE

What is the display for?Internal or external halyard?Which specifications matter?What should the quote include?

What is the display for?

Start with the intended flag, the display position and access for everyday operation. For an existing installation, share the model or product records if available before selecting a replacement pole.

  • Permanent ground display, building-mounted display or portable event setup.
  • Flag dimensions and number of flags in the planned display.
  • Nearby trees, buildings, circulation routes and service access.

Internal or external halyard?

SystemHow it operatesDecision to make
External halyardThe rope runs outside the pole.Where can the cleat be reached and secured?
Internal halyardThe operating system runs inside the pole.Who needs access to the operating point and any keys?
Portable systemThe pole and base form a temporary display.Which surface, footprint and operating conditions are approved?

Which specifications matter?

Compare complete product specifications, not just height or material. Ask for the rated flag capacity, applicable exposure limits, finish, operating hardware and maintenance instructions for the exact model.

A foundation, bracket or base must suit the selected pole and its site. An existing foundation should be assessed before it is reused. Any required engineering, approvals or site preparation should be identified in the installation scope.

What should the quote include?

Separate the pole and hardware from delivery, access equipment, foundation work, installation and ongoing servicing. This makes proposals easier to compare.
